newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Crude output normal at Cano Limon field.
newsitem.headline: Crude output normal at Cano Limon field.

text.p: Crude production at Occidental Petroleum Corp's Cano Limon field in eastern Colombia is "normal" despite a rebel attack on the pipeline that transports oil to the Caribbean coast port of Covenas, a company spokesman said Monday.

The pipeline -- Colombia's largest -- was dynamited by National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas Sunday morning. So far, repair teams have been unable to reach the site of the blast, between the towns of Saravena and Arauquita in Arauca province
ELN rebels shot down a civilian helicopter transporting soldiers to the zone shortly after Sunday's blast, killing 21 soldiers and four civilian crew members.
The spokesman said the extent of the damage to the pipeline was not yet known and no repair timetable had been drawn up.

Occidental has limited storage capacity at its Cano Limon field which is currently producing about 171,000 barrels per day -- down from its average of about 180,000 bpd in the wake of six attacks on the pipeline in the last month.
The spokesman said if the pipeline was not repaired "soon" then production at the field may have to be halted completely.

"The field continues producing because we have some storage capacity but eventually production will be restricted or shut down. It depends how quickly repairs can be carried out," he told Reuters. "That could be in two or three days."
The Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline normally transports about 200,000 bpd along its 487 mile (780 km) length. Sunday's attack by the ELN, Colombia's second largest rebel army, was the 36th this year.
State-run oil company Ecopetrol said in a communique Monday that more than 125,000 barrels of crude were spilled in 35 attacks on the pipeline in the first half of this year.
The bill for repairs, clean-up costs and lost production was put at more than $36 million.
In the 11 years that the 44-inch diameter Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline has been in operation, it has been dynamited 471 times and more than 1.5 million barrels of crude have been spilled.
Ecopetrol puts the total costs of repairs, lost production and environmental damage at $1.6 billion.
